Auxiliary Variables in All-In-One FIML Mediation

Source: vignettes/articles/q_mediation_auxiliary.Rmd
q_mediation_auxiliary.Rmd

Covariates and auxiliary variables

The q_* functions can use aux to add auxiliary variables to an observed-variable FIML mediation model in one call. Variables in cov predict the mediator(s) and/or outcome. Variables in aux are added using the saturated-correlates method implemented by semTools::auxiliary(); they are not added as regression predictors. A variable cannot appear in both roles. A confounder that needs to adjust the substantive equations should therefore be specified in cov, not merely in aux.

An auxiliary variable related to missingness or to an incomplete variable can help make MAR more plausible. Its inclusion does not establish MAR, correct model misspecification, or establish a causal indirect effect. Choose auxiliary variables using knowledge of the study and available data.

A reproducible illustration

This artificial example generates incomplete mediator values, with missingness depending on observed z. The same z also predicts the mediator. It is an illustration of the interface, not a comparison study.

library(manymome)
set.seed(731)
n <- 300
x <- rnorm(n)
c1 <- rnorm(n)
z <- rnorm(n)
m <- 0.5*x + 0.3*c1 + 0.4*z + rnorm(n)
y <- 0.2*x + 0.4*m + 0.2*c1 + rnorm(n)
dat <- data.frame(x, m, y, c1, z)
dat$m[runif(n) < plogis(-1 + 0.5*z)] <- NA

out <- q_simple_mediation(
  x = "x", m = "m", y = "y",
  cov = "c1", aux = "z", data = dat,
  fit_method = "sem", fixed.x = FALSE,
  ci_type = "mc", R = 20000, seed = 123,
  parallel = FALSE, progress = FALSE
)
print(out)

Both equations include c1. Neither equation includes z as a predictor. The fitted likelihood nevertheless includes z through its mean, variance and covariances. Missing values in an auxiliary variable are allowed. Use ci_type = "boot" for nonparametric bootstrap intervals; each resample refits the augmented model. Set an adequate number of resamples for the precision needed in the study.

Settings and scope

Supplying aux treats exogenous variables as random (fixed.x = FALSE). If fixed.x is TRUE, a message announces this change. This introduces distributional assumptions for those variables; it is not just a display option. The printed output identifies the auxiliaries and their role. The path plot displays the substantive mediation model. The full augmented fit can be retrieved with get_fit(out).

This first implementation supports simple, serial, parallel, and custom observed-variable mediation models fitted by SEM with FIML and ML or MLR. Auxiliaries must be numeric, nonconstant, and distinct from the modeled variables. Factor/ordered auxiliary variables, indicators, moderators, SAM, grouped, clustered, weighted, and MI workflows are not supported by this argument. Unsupported combinations produce errors instead of silently ignoring the auxiliary variables. aux = NULL retains the usual workflow.

Auxiliary parameters increase model size. Check convergence, uncertainty, and the number of usable bootstrap resamples, especially with small samples or many correlated auxiliaries.
